stories.summary: Firaxis, the 30-year-old studio behind the Civilization and XCOM franchises, is laying off a third of its staff, totalling 60 people, as reported by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier . Studio head Heather Hazen, who has lead it since 2023 , will be leaving as part of the cuts. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Report: Civilization dev Firaxis lays off a third of its staff
sources.text: 60 people made redundant, including studio head Heather Hazen, as part of "recentering around the studio’s core strength" Firaxis, the 30-year-old studio behind the Civilization and XCOM franchises, is laying off a third of its staff, totalling 60 people, as reported by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier . Studio head Heather Hazen, who has lead it since 2023 , will be leaving as part of the cuts. “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength – designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years,” a spokesperson said in a statement provided to the site. “As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.” The firm previously laid off staff in September 2025 . The studio is reportedly working on a new XCOM title which has "faced development struggles and missed a significant milestone over the summer," according to Schreier, citing internal sources who said the game was still in development but may "face a shakeup" as a result of the staff departures. The last XCOM release, Enemy Unknown 2, was released in 2016; Firaxis shipped Civilization VII last year. Firaxis parent Take-Two Interactive posted net revenue down 16% YoY , but reported GTA 6 pre-orders "far in excess of expectations". A report today from Sensor Tower suggested pre-orders had already topped $1.4B, meaning the title has already exceeded its predecessor's initial three days of revenue in advance of going on sale.

sources.text: Days before GTA 6’s launch, Take-Two has rolled out layoffs at Firaxis Take-Two has rolled out a series of layoffs at Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis. Take-Two confirmed these layoffs in a statement to Bloomberg . The publisher says this restructuring is in aid of focusing on the studio’s “core strength”. However, anonymous employees speaking with the publication state that these layoffs come after development of a new XCOM game had been struggling behind the scenes, missing key milestones. They say that development “may face a shakeup” because of these layoffs. “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studioâs core strength â designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years,” a spokesperson for 2K Games â a subsidiary of Take-Two â told Bloomberg. “As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. “These decisions are never easy, but theyâre essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.” This comes just days before the Take-Two-published GTA 6 is released on PlayStation and Xbox . sources.title: Civilization dev Firaxis reportedly lays off a third of its staff, studio head departs
sources.text: A new XCOM game in development at Firaxis has reportedly struggled and missed a major milestone earlier this year. A Bloomberg report says Civilization studio Firaxis has laid off roughly 60 people, representing about one-third of its total headcount. Heather Hazen, who took over as studio head in 2023 after more than 25 years with Firaxis, is also leaving. A 2K Games spokesperson didn't comment on the reported number of employees let go, but confirmed that layoffs had occurred in a statement provided to PC Gamer. "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," the rep said. "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." The rep also confirmed that Hazen has stepped down as Firaxis studio head: "With the studio entering this reset, she feels this is the right, deliberate moment to hand over the reins to ensure the next studio leader has full ownership of this new era from the start." Firaxis has enjoyed great success as the developer of the Civilization and XCOM games, but it's struggled in recent years. Marvel's Midnight Suns was critically acclaimed but sales were middling, while Civilization 7 was just middling overall: Despite a raft of updates and changes since its 2025 release, its user rating on Steam remains stubbornly "mixed" while player numbers are still well behind that of Civilization 6. That's resulted in previous rounds of layoffs: Roughly 30 people were let go in 2023, while an unknown number were cut in 2025. The Bloomberg report says a new XCOM game in development at Firaxis has also struggled and missed a major milestone earlier this year; work on the game will reportedly continue but may face changes as a result of the layoffs. sources.title: Firaxis lays off 30% of staff with the next XCOM game reportedly struggling
sources.text: It's been six years since the last full-on XCOM installment, and as it turns out, another is in the works. However, I wouldn't get too excited, because, sadly, developer Firaxis Games is reportedly undergoing hefty layoffs, leaving the future of the sci-fi strategy project a tad uncertain. Jason Schreier of Bloomberg is reporting that some 30% of the Firaxis workforce was laid off as of today, November 17. That amounts to somewhere in the region of 60 staff, and owner Take-Two confirmed that Heather Hazen is vacating the role of studio head. People familiar with the matter say a new XCOM is part of the company's current slate, but there have been problems with the game's development of late. These purportedly include failing to hit a major milestone over the summer. Apparently, development of the as-yet-unnamed XCOM will continue, but there may be changes as a result of the rejig. Losing that many devs, it's hard to imagine any games in the works at Firaxis being shielded from some sort of reverberations, however minor or ultimately inconsequential. "Firaxis is restructuring and re-centering around the studio’s core strength - designing world-class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," a statement from Take-Two reads. "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis." These layoffs are occurring on the eve of GTA 6 's release, a tectonic shift across the entire entertainment world. Rockstar, another subsidiary of Take-Two, has been printing money for the last decade-plus thanks to GTA 5 and GTA Online, and is now about to do even more so. How and when this new XCOM is announced remains to be seen. Likewise, questions linger about the ongoing support for Civilization 7 and other entries in the series. sources.title: Xbox's Project Helix "is not a PC that can also play console games"
sources.text: Next Xbox console is "designed to be the ultimate gaming machine" by removing the "arbitrary constraints between console and PC games" Xbox VP of Next Generation Jason Ronald has clarified that Project Helix is "designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games, not a PC that can also play console games." In the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine , Ronald described Project Helix as "the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed." "The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed Project Helix's console and PC compatibility in March, adding that the console will "lead in performance" for Xbox and PC games. As Ronald previously discussed at GDC Festival of Gaming , Project Helix will utilise neural rendering, which uses AI models to enhance graphics. Ronald identified neural rendering as a particular focus for Project Helix, as it also addresses the ongoing component crisis. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and platform designer, it's one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also [making] things accessible and affordable." "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower [and] additional memory." He concluded: "I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last ten years." Reports last month indicated that Project Helix is expected to launch during the 2028 holiday season , with a projected price between $1,200 and $1,800.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
sources.text: "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering." Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable. The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday , and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games. "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation. "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering." While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future , saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future. The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld . "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players." Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

sources.title: Xbox afirma que Project Helix é um console capaz de rodar jogos de PC — e não o contrário
sources.text: A Microsoft divulgou novos detalhes sobre o Project Helix, seu console de nova geração, e reforçou a ideia de que o videogame é capaz de rodar jogos de PC — mas não um PC que consegue rodar jogos de console. Em entrevista publicada na revista especial de 25 anos do Xbox, Jason Ronald, vice-presidente da próxima geração da marca, explicou que o projeto foi desenvolvido para funcionar como um console tradicional, e não como um computador com recursos de videogame. “O Helix foi projetado para ser um console capaz também de rodar jogos do seu PC. Não é um PC que também roda jogos de console”, afirmou Ronald. O executivo também destacou que o aparelho pretende eliminar barreiras entre as bibliotecas de jogos de PC e Xbox, na intenção de manter a experiência simples e intuitiva para os jogadores. Segundo Ronald, a proposta do Project Helix é reunir diferentes bibliotecas em um único dispositivo e permitir com que os jogadores acessem seus títulos com mais facilidade. O console também deve oferecer compatibilidade com quatro gerações de jogos e preservar o progresso das contas Xbox. O executivo explicou que a experiência poderá ser adaptada a diferentes perfis de jogadores. Quem preferir uma experiência tradicional terá acesso rápido aos jogos, enquanto usuários mais avançados poderão personalizar configurações e opções de desempenho. “Quando penso no que torna um console mágico, é o fato de ele tornar meus jogos instantaneamente acessíveis e prontos para jogar”, afirmou Ronald. Ele também destacou que os jogadores não precisarão se preocupar com atualizações de drivers ou configurações típicas de um PC. A ideia, segundo o executivo, é criar uma plataforma que reúna a praticidade dos consoles com a flexibilidade dos computadores. “Quando pensamos no Project Helix, ele foi realmente concebido para ser a máquina de jogos definitiva — uma que remove todas as barreiras de jogo que existiram historicamente”, declarou. Durante a entrevista, Ronald também comentou sobre os desafios de desenvolver um novo console em meio à crise de componentes de PC. Segundo ele, a Microsoft está investindo em tecnologias como a renderização neural para melhorar o desempenho sem exigir mais poder computacional ou memória. “É definitivamente um momento desafiador, mas, como designer de sistemas e plataformas, também é um dos momentos mais empolgantes”, afirmou. O executivo explicou que a equipe busca novas soluções para avançar tecnologicamente e, ao mesmo tempo, manter os custos de produção e os preços sustentáveis. Ronald citou a renderização neural como uma das principais apostas para a próxima geração. A tecnologia pode abranger diferentes técnicas de processamento de imagem, como aprimoramento de resolução, geração de quadros e reconstrução de iluminação, embora a Microsoft ainda não tenha detalhado como pretende aplicá-la no Project Helix. O executivo também afirmou que a próxima geração não deve ser definida apenas por especificações tradicionais — como resolução 8K ou taxas de atualização de 240 Hz. Para ele, o foco estará em novas experiências de jogo, maior imersão e avanços visuais mais eficientes. E você, está ansioso para conhecer a próxima geração de consoles? sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) Dinkytowns aside, what San Andreas does better than GTA 5 is space - the peculiar flat spaces of Southern California in particular, a state in which you can never quite tell where the wilderness ends and the landscaping begins, and where the ancient rocks that announce the horizon can look new, like stage settings, while the freeways feel truly ancient, concrete lizards sleeping on the dirt, bleached by the easy sun. sources.title: We got GTA 6 nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards before GTA 6
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Resident Evil Requiem join it in competition for the top award The Game Awards 2026 nominations are in, and would you believe it, GTA 6 has been nominated for Game of the Year. GTA 6 isn't out until later this week and it's now up for Game of the Year alongside seven other awards at the Keighleys, which is set to air on Thursday December 10, 2026. We don't even have reviews for Rockstar's latest yet, but I guess that's a good sign that it'll be pretty good when it arrives later this week. The nominees for The Game Awards Game of the Year are GTA 6, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , Resident Evil Requiem, 007 First Light, Phantom Blade Zero, and Control Resonant. Meanwhile, other potential Game of the Year candidates like Pragmata, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and Pokemon: Pokopia have been represented in the genre categories. As for the penultimate award for Best Game Direction, unsurprisingly Rockstar and Capcom are in the category with GTA 6 and Resident Evil Requiem respectively. But Capcom pulled out another nomination in this category with Pragmata, Remedy for Control Resonant, and S-Game for Phantom Blade Zero also in the running. While games like God of War Ragnarok and Dragon Age Inquisition were released pretty close to the cutoff date, this marks the first time that a game that hasn't released yet has been nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards. sources.text: "What if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games?" I imagine most BioWare fans would argue that the studio's peak happened somewhere between Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect 2. For me, though, the absolute high point was Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and I was always a little bitter that the devs moved on to create Mass Effect rather than finishing Revan's story in a proper KOTOR 3. That's why seeing Casey Hudson, original director of KOTOR, return with a spiritual successor in Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic is so exciting, and it's apparently been a long time coming. "It is really a dream project for us," Hudson says in an interview with The Fourth Curtain podcast . After leaving BioWare – for a second time – in 2020, he founded a new studio called Humanoid Origin, which was developing a "sci-fi action RPG" that would've been a "brand-new IP." That studio shuttered in 2024 after an "unexpected shortfall of funding," leaving Hudson to figure out what to do next. "We had lots of ideas, including, like, 'Do we get funding to continue with what we were doing? Are there other paths forward?' But over the years – myself and folks from our team, we worked on the original Knights of the Old Republic way back in the day, and since then BioWare also had the Old Republic MMO. So we've kept up connections with folks at Lucasfilm ," he says. Some time after Humanoid Origin shut down, Hudson explains, "the head of Disney Games reached out and said, 'Hey, what if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games? The spiritual successor.'" Hudson says he'd been "circling" the idea of returning to KOTOR for some time. "It's something that I would love to do, but I was either doing other things or other projects. There were times when maybe it wasn't right for Lucasfilm, or they weren't ready for it. There wasn't really a fit." He was excited both by the possibility of returning to KOTOR and bringing back "some of the the top folks we've worked with," but surviving a studio shutdown leads you to "become the most skeptical person on earth," he says. "You don't really trust anyone to follow through with a deal or funding until things are signed, done, and legit." Getting those contracts finalized is how Hudson spent "the first half" of 2025. Then he spent the rest of the year "just starting to assemble our team, doing a prototype, and then creating the announcement trailer." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Yes, that means that Fate of the Old Republic had only barely entered development at the time of its reveal at The Game Awards last year, but Hudson seems confident we won't be waiting forever for it to be finished. The team works "at a very brisk pace," and he says we should expect "new announcements" sometime next year. Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic could be going for "a more simple hero's journey" to avoid BioWare's "self-indulgent" storytelling, says ex-Dragon Age boss Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Sony Defeats $2.6 Billion Class-Action Lawsuit Over Claimed PlayStation Store Monopoly
sources.text: Since 2022 , Sony has been facing the British equivalent of a class action lawsuit that could have cost the company as much as $2.6 billion had it lost. It, however, did not. As reported byÂ The Game Business , the lawsuit brought by consumer advocate Alex Neill claimed that Sony was operating a “near monopoly” via the PlayStation Store, and sued the Japanese company on behalf of nine million UK PlayStation owners, but today the claims were rejected, and the case has been dismissed. The reported financial goal of the lawsuit has wildly swung about over the years, cited as $5.9 billion in 2022 , then $7.9 billion by 2023 , and then down to $2.6 billion in May of this year. Whatever the number, the case being made was that by not allowing third-party stores to sell digital PlayStation games, Sony effectively has a monopoly from which it extracts 30 percent of every sale. This, said Neill and the PlayStation You Owe Us campaign, was an “abuse” of Sony’s “dominant position,” forcing customers to pay “too much for digital games and in-game content purchased through the PlayStation Store.” A previous attempt to have the case thrown out was rejected in 2023, and then things looked far worse for Sony when it lost a very similar case in California in May of this year , to the tune of $7.8 billion. And there’s the rather pertinent point that Sony absolutely does dominate sales of digital games on PlayStation, and that’s only going to get a whole lot worse as the megacorp phases out physical media entirely. Yet, following May’s trial , London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has rejected the argument and ruled that, as reported by TGB , “the claim failed to establish that PlayStation infringed competition law.” The argument against a monopoly was based on the wider competition of Xbox, Nintendo, and PC, alongside the (current) option to buy physical versions of games. Allowing third-party stores onto the PlayStation could, the court said, impact security, which interestingly was the failed argument Google made in its battle against Epic. The tribunal also said Neill had failed to prove that Sony’s profits were “excessive,” likely given that 30 percent cuts are pretty much an industry standard. sources.title: PlayStation beats $2.6 billion lawsuit over its game prices
sources.text: PlayStation will not be compelled to allow third-party stores on its consoles A lawsuit brought against PlayStation over its storefront and game prices has been dismissed. The UK class action lawsuit was brought against PlayStation by Alex Neill,Â representing PlayStation users who complained that they were trapped and forced to use the PS Store. They argued that PlayStation’s 30% cut on all game sales led to games being sold for “excessive and unfair prices”. If PlayStation lost the lawsuit, the plaintiffs were seeking $2.6 billion in damages. As reported by The Game Business , Londonâs Competition Appeal Tribunal has rejected this argument entirely, dismissing the idea that PlayStation has a “near monopoly” on the market. However, part of its argument was that users could instead opt to buy games physically – something which will not remain the case for much longer. PlayStation says it will phase out physical game sales by January 2028 . With that said, PlayStation users might not have much more luck with this argument when physical games are phased out either. That is because the court was not convinced that PlayStation games were priced too highly on the PS Store, or that game prices would be brought down if PlayStation allowed third-party storefronts on its systems.Â PlayStation is facing similar lawsuits in other regions, so it remains to be seen if it can defeat all of them. If any of them were to side against the company, that could set a significant precedent in the gaming industry, opening all platform owners up to third-party storefronts. For the time being, though, the status quo has been maintained with this UK ruling. Right now, the big three console giants – PlayStation, Xbox , and Nintendo – all maintain their own storefronts on their platforms. The only exception to this is Valve , which allows users to buy games from other storefronts on the Steam Machine and Steam Deck. Xbox’s storefront is also available on PC , as is Xbox Game Pass.

sources.title: London court tosses $2.6 billion Sony lawsuit claiming it holds "near monopoly" on PlayStation Store
sources.text: The case was dismissed entirely and unanimously A $2.6 billion lawsuit alleging Sony holds a "near monopoly" through the PlayStation Store, and has used its position to charge more and extract "unfair" margins on sales, has been dismissed by the London Competition Appeal Tribunal. As The Game Business spotted, the class action-style case case was dismissed entirely via unanimous judgment . "The Class Representative has not satisfied us that Sony is dominant in any relevant market for the purposes of assessing any anti-competitive infringement by Sony," the concluding remarks read. The question was not whether Sony is dominant on the PlayStation Store. Of course Sony is king on its own platform. The court essentially examined whether that dominance creates or supports unfair, illegally monopolistic conditions. The court ruled that it does not, and for a variety of factors, including competition provided by physical game sales, as well as platforms like Xbox, Nintendo, and PC. Additionally, it found that letting third-party stores on the PlayStation platform would require "significant adaptation of the platform and its operations" at "significant cost and effort," likely leading to "reduced security in the platform architecture and with potentially reduced performance." The impending end of physical PlayStation games, with Sony looking to phase out discs for new games in January 2028, obviously looms over the discussion here. The court did acknowledge it, but only via post-trial submissions, as this lawsuit stretches back to 2022, far before Sony announced the end of discs. But I do think the court's comments are relevant and interesting in general. "If there is no substitution between physical and digital games, then a decision to cease physical sales would mean that those sales would be lost altogether," one snippet reads. "If there is a legitimate concern with this decision, it would be (contrary to the Class Representative's case) that it eliminates a competitive constraint on Sony from independent retailers and allows Sony to increase digital pricing once that constraint has gone." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more That is, indeed, one concern with the end of discs: the physical market not only provides a potentially cheaper option and resale path, its existence also puts a leash on digital prices. Pertinently, Nintendo is selling some Switch 2 games $10 cheaper digitally as it reduces but does not remove its physical footprint in today's game-key card era. In the chunky court document, a whole SSNIP analysis – "A small, but significant, non-transitory increase in price of 5-10% – looks at whether "physical games are a substitute for digital games" and if such a digital price increase would drive PlayStation users to physical. Of course, we know where the court landed. Additionally, the judgment reads, "Even if Nintendo and gaming PCs are not within the relevant market, we think it very likely that they impose a constraint on the behaviour of both Sony and Microsoft . There is abundant evidence that Sony sees both as a competitive threat." All of this and more seems to fold into the conclusion: the PlayStation Store's 30% sales cut is not uncommon (just ask Steam), its pricing wasn't found to be unfair, consumers have many alternatives to Sony's store (currently including physical), and other platforms indirectly enforce price parity by offering user choice. With Sony facing similar cases elsewhere , it'll be interesting to see how lawsuits like this evolve assuming PlayStation ends discs as planned. Eyes will also be glued to PlayStation Store pricing and policy up to and especially after January 2028. PlayStation is "hearing the feedback from customers" on discs, says JRPG boss whose business is built on physical games. Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Coming to XBOX Game Pass: Hela: of Mice & Magic, The Outlast Trials, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2, and More
sources.text: Gather around, gamers! We’ve got more games coming your way, and there’s a little something for everyone. In the mood for a little magic? Terrifying trials? High-stakes sniper missions? We’ve got it all. So, let’s get right into the games! Paw Patrol: Dino World (Cloud, Console, and PC) Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass Embark on a dino-sized action adventure in Paw Patrol Dino World ! Explore Dino Island, rescue dinosaurs, overcome obstacles using the Pups’ unique skills and put a stop to Mayor Humdinger’s chaos. Take on the adventure solo or team up with a friend in two-player co-op. Call of the Elder Gods (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) – November 18 Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass Journey to the far corners of the Earth and unearth ancient horrors in this Lovecraftian narrative puzzle adventure and sequel to 2020’s critically acclaimed Call of the Sea . High on Life 2 (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) – November 18 Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass An intergalactic conspiracy threatens the fate of humanity! Team up with a wide cast of talking alien guns as you shoot, stab, and skate your way through exotic locales across the galaxy to take down the bad guys and save your favorite species (humans)! Roadside Research (Game Preview) (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) – November 18 Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass Aliens have landed on Earth… to run a gas station. Play solo or up to 4 players doing human tasks to blend in. Scan, steal, and test various methods on customers while they stop by the gas station. Gather all data you can from humans without raising the suspicion meter too high, risk a visit from government officials. Black Jacket (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) – November 19 Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass 21 or eternity? Black Jacket drops you into a purgatorial card game where restless souls wager their coins, and the ferryman waits for his cut. From Mi’pu’mi Games and Skystone Games ( Tiny Bookshop ) — a painterly, pitch-black spin on blackjack awaits. Cheating fully encouraged. Motorslice (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) – November 24 Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass Play as the skilled (but seemingly ever-sleepy) slicer, P, and parkour through the ruins of a brutalist megastructure, climb massive bosses, and hunt down every piece of living construction equipment in this slice of life action-adventure with immaculate vibes. Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) – November 24 Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is a modern warfare shooter set in the Middle East. Play as Raven, contract sniper assassin, as you take out a series of targets across a dramatic single-player campaign. With extreme-range shots exceeding 1000m, gear up for the most challenging entry to the series yet. Arkheron (Game Preview) (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, and PC) – November 27 Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass Available on day one with XBOX Game Pass! Enter Arkheron , a fast-paced PvP action game where teams of three scale a mysterious Tower. Items are the heroes – imbued with abilities that define your strategy. Loot, adapt, and strategize your playstyle on the fly. Every decision alters how you fight and who you become. Ascension awaits. The Outlast Trials (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, and PC) – December 1 Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass In The Outlast Trials , human guinea pigs are recruited by the Murkoff Corporation to test methods of brainwashing and mind control. In a world of fear and horror, your morals will be stretched to their limits, and your sanity crushed. Survive alongside friends or dare to face the experiments alone. Hela: of Mice & Magic (Cloud, XBOX Series X|S, and PC) – December 1 Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass Available on day one with XBOX Game Pass! See the world through the eyes of a brave little mouse in this enchanting 3D co-op adventure. Explore breathtaking landscapes inspired by Northern Sweden, solve puzzles, and be a force for good in a land where heartwarming storytelling and the beauty of nature intertwine. World of Tanks Blitz – Monthly Bonus (PC) – December 1 Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, Game Pass Essential, PC Game Pass Join World of Tanks Blitz ! Choose from 700+ historical and fantasy vehicles and battle across 30+ arenas in over 10 modes. Team up with friends, join clans, compete in tournaments, and earn rewards! Enjoy welcome rewards and monthly bundles with XBOX Game Pass! World of Tanks Modern Armor – XP Stock (Console) – December 1 Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, Game Pass Essential Stay ahead of the competition with this exclusive bundle, specially crafted for Game Pass subscribers! It’s packed with powerful rewards that will help you dominate even the toughest challenges, so don’t miss this chance to gear up and roll right into battle, Commander! Here’s what you’ll find in this bundle: 3 Days of Premium Account, x4 Commander XP Boosters (6), x3 Vehicle XP (6). The following games are leaving the Game Pass library soon. Don’t want the fun to end? Save on these games now before they leave Game Pass! Well, that should keep you busy for a while! Enjoy exploring the lineup – we hope you discover something new to love. Keep an eye on social for more news and updates, and we’ll catch you next time! Note: Games with a ‘Handheld’ designation represent those that are optimized for handheld play.

sources.text: Chega mais, gamers! Temos mais jogos a caminho, com um pouco de tudo para todos os gostos. A fim de um pouco de magia? Provações aterrorizantes? Missões de franco-atirador em que há muito em jogo? Temos tudo isso. Então, vamos direto aos jogos! Patrulha Canina: O Mundo dos Dinossauros (nuvem, console e PC) Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium e PC Game Pass Embarque em uma aventura de ação de proporções jurássicas em Patrulha Canina: O Mundo dos Dinossauros! Explore a Ilha dos Dinossauros, resgate-os, supere obstáculos usando as habilidades únicas dos filhotes e dê um fim à confusão causada pelo prefeito Humdinger. Encare a aventura solo ou junte-se a um amigo no modo cooperativo para dois jogadores. Call of the Elder Gods (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S, portátil e PC) 18 de novembro – agora no Game Pass Premium (já disponível nos planos Ultimate e PC Game Pass) Viaje aos confins da Terra e descubra horrores ancestrais nesta aventura narrativa de quebra-cabeças de inspiração lovecraftiana, sequência de Call of the Sea , lançado em 2020 e aclamado pela crítica. High on Life 2 (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S, portátil e PC) 18 de novembro – agora no Game Pass Premium (já disponível nos planos Ultimate e PC Game Pass) Uma conspiração intergaláctica ameaça o destino da humanidade! Junte-se a um elenco variado de armas alienígenas falantes e abra caminho pela galáxia com tiros, facadas e manobras de skate, explorando locais exóticos para derrotar os vilões e salvar sua espécie favorita (os humanos)! Roadside Research (Game Preview) (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S, portátil e PC) 18 de novembro – agora no Game Pass Premium (já disponível nos planos Ultimate e PC Game Pass) Alienígenas chegaram à Terra… para administrar um posto de gasolina. Jogue solo ou em um grupo de até quatro jogadores e realize tarefas humanas para se misturar. Escaneie, roube e teste diferentes métodos nos clientes que passam pelo posto. Colete o máximo de dados possível sobre os humanos sem deixar o medidor de suspeita subir demais, ou você corre o risco de receber uma visita de agentes do governo. Black Jacket (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S, portátil e PC) 19 de novembro – agora no Game Pass Premium (já disponível nos planos Ultimate e PC Game Pass) 21 ou a eternidade? Black Jacket coloca você em um jogo de cartas no purgatório, onde almas inquietas apostam suas moedas e o barqueiro espera pela parte dele. Um jogo da Mi’pu’mi Games e da Skystone Games ( Tiny Bookshop ), essa é uma versão profundamente sombria do jogo de cartas 21, com visual de pintura, e espera por você. Trapacear é mais do que permitido: é incentivado. Motorslice (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S, portátil e PC) 24 de novembro – agora no Game Pass Premium (já disponível nos planos Ultimate e PC Game Pass) Neste jogo brasileiro, jogue na pele de P, especialista em cortes que parece estar sempre com sono, e pratique parkour pelas ruínas de uma megaestrutura brutalista, escale chefes gigantescos e cace todas as máquinas de construção vivas nesta aventura de ação com toques de cotidiano e uma vibe impecável. Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 (nuvem, console, portátil e PC) 24 de novembro – Game Pass Ultimate, Premium e PC Game Pass Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 é um jogo de tiro de guerra moderna ambientado no Oriente Médio. Assuma o papel de Raven, um franco-atirador de aluguel, e elimine uma série de alvos ao longo de uma intensa campanha solo. Com disparos de alcance extremo que ultrapassam 1.000 metros, prepare-se para o jogo mais desafiador da série até agora. Arkheron (Game Preview) (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S e PC) 27 de novembro – Game Pass Ultimate e PC Game Pass Disponível no primeiro dia no XBOX Game Pass! Entre em Arkheron , um jogo de ação PvP de ritmo acelerado em que equipes de três jogadores escalam uma Torre misteriosa. Os itens são os protagonistas: imbuídos de habilidades, eles definem sua estratégia. Colete saques, adapte-se e ajuste seu estilo de jogo em tempo real. Cada decisão muda a forma como você luta e quem você se torna. A ascensão espera por você. The Outlast Trials (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S e PC) 1 de dezembro – Game Pass Ultimate, Premium e PC Game Pass Em The Outlast Trials , cobaias humanas são recrutadas pela Corporação Murkoff para testar métodos de lavagem cerebral e controle mental. Em um mundo de medo e horror, seus princípios morais serão levados ao limite, e sua sanidade será destruída. Sobreviva ao lado de amigos ou ouse enfrentar os experimentos por conta própria. Hela: of Mice & Magic (nuvem, XBOX Series X|S e PC) 1 de dezembro – Game Pass Ultimate e PC Game Pass Disponível no primeiro dia no XBOX Game Pass! Veja o mundo pelos olhos de um corajoso ratinho nesta encantadora aventura cooperativa em 3D. Explore paisagens deslumbrantes inspiradas no norte da Suécia, resolva quebra-cabeças e faça o bem em uma terra onde histórias emocionantes e a beleza da natureza se entrelaçam. World of Tanks Blitz – bônus mensal (PC) 1 de dezembro – Game Pass Ultimate, Premium, Essential e PC Game Pass Entre em World of Tanks Blitz ! Escolha entre mais de 700 veículos históricos e de fantasia e batalhe em mais de 30 arenas, com mais de 10 modos de jogo. Junte-se a amigos, entre em clãs, dispute torneios e ganhe recompensas! Aproveite recompensas de boas-vindas e pacotes mensais com o XBOX Game Pass! World of Tanks Modern Armor – estoque de XP (console) 1 de dezembro – Game Pass Ultimate, Premium e Essential Fique à frente da concorrência com este pacote exclusivo, criado especialmente para assinantes do Game Pass! Ele está repleto de recompensas poderosas que vão ajudar você a superar até os desafios mais difíceis. Não perca a chance de se equipar e partir direto para a batalha, Comandante! Confira o que você encontrará neste pacote: 3 dias de Conta Premium, 6 bônus de EXP de Comandante x4 e 6 bônus de EXP de veículo x3. Os jogos a seguir deixarão o catálogo do Game Pass em breve. Não quer que a diversão acabe? Aproveite para comprar esses jogos com desconto antes que saia
